Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the detailed traffic shapes last week. I pulled together a short playbook and the scenario model (attached) that maps Novara's deal targets to a recommended Dedicated footprint and operational runbook. High-level summary up front:

- Baseline request profile you sent: average prompt+response = ~1,200 tokens; peak QPS observed in pilot = 10 (short bursts to 30)
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end latency <= 300ms for interactive use-cases; asynchronous batch can tolerate higher
- Recommended initial Dedicated footprint: 3 x A100-class GPUs (quantized 13B model path) with autoscale to 6 during sustained bursts and 12 for short peaks (30s–2m) using burst pool.

Key throughput math (see attached CSV for scenario rows):
- Tokens/sec demand (avg) = avg_tokens_per_request * QPS = 1,200 * 10 = 12,000 tok/s
- Modeling throughput per GPU (13B q4_0 path, seq 1,024 typical) = ~6k tok/s (measured on our infra for this workload)
- GPUs needed (avg) = ceil(12,000 / 6,000) = 2 -> we recommend 3 to provide 50% headroom for variability and to absorb batching inefficiencies
- Peak bursts (30 QPS sustained for 2m) -> 1,200 * 30 = 36,000 tok/s -> burst capacity required = 36,000 / 6,000 = 6 GPUs -> add burst slack to 12 (2x multiplier) to cover p95 latency targets during cold-cache and heavy KV cache pressure

SLO fit and latency considerations:
- p95 latency target (300ms) implies strict limits on queueing and batching window. For interactive path we cap per-request batching to 40ms and set max batch size to avoid per-token emission stalls.
- Model variant tradeoffs:
  - 13B quantized gives best tokens/sec per GPU (~6k) with acceptable quality for your classification-heavy prompts.
  - 70B pruned/quant path reduces req/sec (1.4k tok/s), increasing GPU counts by ~4x but improves answer fidelity for generative flows. Recommend dual-variant routing: route bounded/structured inference to 13B variant, route long-form generation to 70B on fallback.

Operational runbook (short):
1) Provision 3 dedicated GPUs in primary pool + 6 in burst pool (reserved but cold until used).
2) Configure autoscaler: scale up to burst pool when 1-minute rolling token consumption > 80% of baseline pool capacity.
3) Enable prefix/KV cache for session-affine flows to reduce tokens emitted and lower effective tokens/sec by ~12–18%.
4) Canary rollout: start traffic at 10% for 48h, monitor token invoicing, p95 latencies, and top-of-queue time.
5) Add automatic fallback to 13B when latency SLO is threatened; log quality deltas and revert/alert if regressions exceed threshold in your eval set.
